slides.text: Types of data, and why they matter
slides.say: Data Science from Scratch, lesson two: the types of data, and why they matter.

slides.text: The type of data decides what you can do with it.
slides.say: Before you analyse anything, you need to know what kind of data you have. The type decides which charts, statistics, and models make sense.

slides.sub: Tables with rows and columns · text, images, audio
slides.say: First, the big split. Structured data fits neatly into tables, with rows and columns, like a spreadsheet. Unstructured data doesn't: think text, images, and audio.

slides.sub: Number of loans · a person's height
slides.say: Numerical data comes in two kinds. Discrete data is counted, like the number of loans someone has taken. Continuous data is measured, like a person's height, and can take any value in a range.

slides.text:
Nominal: no order
Ordinal: has an order
slides.sub: City, payment method · low, medium, high risk
slides.say: Categorical data puts things into groups. Nominal categories have no natural order, like city or payment method. Ordinal categories do have an order, like low, medium, and high risk.

slides.text: Averaging categories that are stored as numbers
slides.sub: If 1 = Lagos and 2 = Abuja, an 'average city' of 1.5 means nothing.
slides.say: A classic beginner mistake: treating categories as numbers just because they're stored as numbers. If one means Lagos and two means Abuja, an average city of one point five means nothing.

slides.text: Know your data type before you analyse.
slides.say: So the takeaway: always check your data types before you analyse.
